correctness.rationale: The rank-one resolvent identity and signed eigenbasis update hold for every positive step. Conditioning yields the exact mean, zero cross moment, and two-dimensional positive moment matrix; Cayley–Hamilton gives the closed finite-N variance. For \(h=T/N\), the fast-direction random error is \(O(h)\) in \(L^2\), the slow-direction linearized independent Rademacher array has variance tending to \(V>0\), its replacement error is \(O(h^{3/2})\) in \(L^2\), and Lindeberg–Slutsky yield a one-direction Gaussian limit. Its second moment tends to the same explicit nonzero coefficient, proving rate sharpness. The packaged checker exhausts sign histories for multiple rational parameter choices and confirms the coefficient numerically.

value.rationale: The exact finite-step damping/noise covariance and sharp nonzero continuous-time variance are natural quantitative error invariants for the source randomized integrator, not a contrived parameter cutoff. The explicit fast-to-slow mode transfer explains anisotropy of splitting error, yields a one-dimensional confidence diagnostic, and demonstrates that the general half-order guarantee cannot be improved for noncommuting linear components without extra conditions.
